out.other_title: Self-critiquing models: model-written critiques help humans find flaws in summaries
out.rationale: Saunders et al. fine-tune models with behavioural cloning to write critiques that help humans find flaws in summaries. McAleese et al. train critic models with RLHF to write critiques of model-written code, using adversarially inserted bugs as references, and report critiques preferred over human critiques in 63% of cases on natural errors.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: model-written critiques that help humans evaluate model outputs, extended from supervised summarisation critics to RLHF-trained code critics

text: The authors train 'critic' models, LLMs trained with RLHF to write natural-language feedback highlighting problems in code from real-world assistant tasks, to help humans evaluate model-written code more accurately. They report that on code with naturally occurring LLM errors model critiques are preferred over human critiques in 63% of cases, and that human evaluation finds models catch more bugs than human contractors paid for code review.
title: CriticGPT: RLHF-trained LLM critics help humans evaluate model-written code
